comment.narrative: During the projects inception phase the global team developed impact indicators to measure the perceived levels of horizontal and vertical accountability in the sector or institution targeted by the SANCUS partner in each country. Drawing on academic literature the indicators operationalised two core characteristics of both vertical and horizontal accountability focusing on the quality of inclusion and responsiveness of duty bearers under vertical accountability and the independence and answerability of oversight institutions under horizontal accountability. The team developed a fivepoint accountability scale for each of the four variables. The criteria were broad enough to encompass all 26 national SANCUS interventions but specific enough to distinguish between different values. Based on these variables an expert survey tailored to each project country was developed. This meant that the survey questions in each country were applied to the particular area of intervention such as specific sectors and institutions targeted by SANCUS for instance the education sector in Armenia or municipal governments in Palestine. This allowed the project team to better understand the changes in the areas in which SANCUS was active and to therefore capture contributions made by the intervention.The survey was circulated to incountry experts and partners in each country and translated into four languages to expand its reach. The experts which included academics journalists businesspeople CSO representatives and retired officials ranked the four variables on the 15 scale once at the beginning of the project in each country and once at the end. The project team then aggregated and averaged the score for each variable and compared the baseline and endline results.This provided a robust basis for evaluating changes in the quality of vertical and horizontal accountability within the specific intervention areas of each SANCUS project country at the conclusion of the Action. According to the results 17 countrieslocations experienced an increased level of horizontal accountability including Armenia Bosnia and Herzegovina Brazil Cameroon the Gambia Honduras Indonesia Jordan Kenya Lebanon Maldives Morocco Nigeria Panama Rwanda Zambia Zimbabwe.However there were also declines in the perceived quality of horizontal accountability in 7 countrieslocations including Cambodia Chile Colombia Guatemala Jamaica Palestine Sri Lanka.
